text.S1: Near a great forest dwelt a poor woodcutter with his wife and his two children. The boy was called Hansel and the girl Gretel.

text.T1: Kwa tuko a mushitu wo mutuna nekupila muuna wa mubotana yanapila kakupumaka likota. Na pila ni musalaa hae ni bana bababeli. Mushimani neli Hazelu mi musizana neli Kilitelu.
text.T2: Kwatuko ni mushitu womutuna neku pila muuna wa mubotana yanaa pila ka kupumaka likota. Naa pila ni musalaahae ni bana bababeli. Mushimani neeli Hanselu mi musizana neeli Giritelu.
text.To: Ibat'o ba mwa mushitu o mutuna ne ku inzi likota ze maswe ni musal'a hae ni bana ba hae ba babeli.
text.So: There, a poor man living with his wife and two sons lived in a small forest, surrounded by a poor man who lived with a tree.

text.T1: Nana ni zenyinyni za kulima ni kuloba, mi linanga lelituna haliwezi fafasi, na sakoni kuleka sinkwa zazi ni zazi. Cwale hato hupula zataba ye busihu halobezi fa mumbeta, mi kia iposa kuba pilaelo ya hae.
text.T2: Naana ni zenyinyani za kuca ni kushanyauna, mi linanga lelituna hali taha mwa naha, naa sakoni kuleka buhobe bwa zazi ni zazi. Cwale haato nahana za buino bo busihu halobezi fa mumbeta, ni kuposa pilaelo yahae.
text.To: N'a si na hande za ku luma ni ku feza, mi ha n'a wile mwa muleneñi o mutuna, n'a sa koni ku fumana buhobe bwa ka zazi ni zazi. Cwale ha n'a nahana fa mumbeta wa hae, ni ku bilaela za hae.
text.So: He had little food and no rain, and when a severe drought came into the land, he could not afford the bread for the day; then he could not afford this night's bread when he was lying in bed, and he would have his worry.

text.S1: He groaned and said to his wife, “What is to become of us? How are we to feed our poor children, when we no longer have anything even for ourselves?”
text.S2: He groaned and said to his wife, “What is to become of us? How are we to feed our poor children, when we no longer have anything even for ourselves?”
text.T1: Atongoka mi ali kumusalaa hae, kin͂i sesitaha kuluna? Luka uta cwani bana baluna bababotana haiba alusana ni haiba saluna feela?
text.T2: Atongokela musalaahae ali, “Ki n͂i sesi lukenela? Luka uta cwañi bana baluna bababotana haiba nji halusana ni haiba saluna feela?”
text.To: U seha ni ku bulelela musal'a hae, u li: Lu ka fepa cwañi bana ba luna ba ba shebile, hailif'o ha lu sa na nihaiba se siñwi ku luna?
text.So: He cried out to his wife, "I'm a little boy, and how can we raise our children if we don't have to be here? "

text.S1: “I’ll tell you what, husband,” answered the woman, “Early tomorrow morning we will take the children out into the forest where it is the thickest. There we will light a fire for them, and give each of them one piece of bread, and then we will go to our work and leave them alone. They will not find the way home again, and we shall be rid of them.”

text.S1: When day dawned, but before the sun had risen, the woman came and awoke the two children, saying, “Get up, you sluggards! We are going into the forest to fetch wood.” She gave each a little piece of bread, and said, “There is something for your dinner, but do not eat it up before then, for you will get nothing else.”

Lwaya mwa mushitu kuyo bata likota. “Afa yomumwi ni yomumwi kaemba ka sinkwa, mi ali, “kuna ni sico sa mulalelo, kono musike mwaca pili, kakuli hakuna se mukafiwa.”

Luya mwa mushitu kuyo lwalela likota.” Afa yomuñwi ni yomuñwi kaemba ka buhobe, mi ali, “Kuna ni sico sa mulalelo, kono musike mwasica pili, kakuli hakuna semuka fiwa.”

text.T1: Hazelu ni Kilitelu baina kwa tuko a mulilo, mi kweli haiyo taha, man͂i ni man͂i anga kaemba ka kanyinyani ka sinkwa, mi aba toutwa mulumo wa kota yeteta kuwa baumela kuli ndataa bona ufakaufi. Nesi cwalo nihakulicwalo, capu, neli mutai woo natamezi kwa kota ye ne omile wonofukiswa ki moya wono fulana. Mi hane bainzi nako ye telele, meeto abona akwaela ni mabote, mi baya fa buloko kapili. Cwale kwa mafelelezo a ba totona, seli busihu mwa lififi.
text.T2: Hanselu ni Giritelu baina kwatuko ni mulilo, mi hase kuli musihali, man͂i ni man͂i aanga kaemba kakanyinyani ka buhobe, mi haba utwa mulumo wa capu kota yelema kota, balumela kuli ndataabona ufakaufi. Kanti neesi cwalo kuli neeli capu yene bautwa kono neeli mutai wone atamezi kwa kota yene iomile wone ufukiswa ki moya wonoo fulana. text.So: They walked all night and came up to their father's house, knocked at his door, and the woman looked at the door as Hanselu and Gilusa, the little children, had been out for a long time in the forest, and we thought they had never come back!

text.S1: The father, however, rejoiced, for it had cut him to the heart to leave them behind alone. Not long afterwards, there was once more great scarcity in all parts, and the children heard their mother saying at night to their father, “Everything is eaten again, we have one half loaf left, and after that there is no more. The children must go. We will take them farther into the wood, so that they will not find their way out again; there is no other means of saving ourselves!”

They did not awake until it was dark night, and Hansel comforted his little sister and said, “Just wait, Gretel, until the moon rises, and then we shall see the crumbs of bread which I have strewn about, they will show us our way home again.” When the moon came they set out, but they found no crumbs.

text.T1: Baken͂isa bo lule ban͂ata ba linyunywani ba basweli ku fufa-fufa kwa likota ni masimu libunopile kaufela. Hazelu abulela ku kilitelu, “katuha lufumana nzila onafa,” kono neba sika ifumana. Neba zamaile busihu kaufela mane ni lizazi lelitatama kuzwa kakusasana kuyofita mazibwana, bapalelwa kuzwa mwa mushitu, mi neba nshwile ahulu tala, bakin͂isa kuli neba sina sakuca kwanda miselo ye mibeli kapa yemilalu yene melile fa fasi. Cwale hane bakatezi cwalo kuli mane mahutu abona akuna kwa nakabaisa, balobala mwaatasa kota ni kuya fa buloko.
text.T2: Ki baken͂isa bolule baban͂ata-ñata ba linyunywani babasweli kufufa-fufa kwa likota ni masimu mi libunopile buhobe kaufelaabona. Bashwa hahulu tala baken͂isa kuli neba sina sakuca kwandaa miselo yemibeli kapa yemilaalu yene imelile fafasi. Cwale hane bakatezi cwalo kuli mane mahutu abona hakuna kwanaa kabayisa, balobala mwaatasa kota ni kuya fa buloko.
text.To: Bo Hansel ne ba bulelezi linyunywani ze ñata - ñata ze ne fufanga mwa mushitu ni mwa masimu kaufela kuli li yo fita ni kakusasana, mi kapili - pili ne ba bulezi kuli ne lu ka fumana nzila, ne lu si ka i fumana, kono ne ba si ka i fumana; ne ba zamaya busihu kaufela ni musihali ku zwa kakusasana ku isa manzibwana, kono ne ba si ka zwa mwa mushitu, mi ne ba lapile hahulu, kakuli ne ba sa ci se siñwi, mi ne ba sa koni ku lobala fafasi, mi ne ba sa koni ku lobala mwateñi.
text.So: Among the thousands of birds walking from trees and fields, Hanse said that the ground would soon run the way, and they would go all night long until dawns and even go out of the forest, so that they could not eat as much as they would do when they would eat any fruit from it.

text.S1: It was now three mornings since they had left their father’s house. text.S1: The duck came to them, and Hansel seated himself on its back, and told his sister to sit by him. “No,” replied Gretel, “that will be too heavy for the little duck; she shall take us across, one after the other.” The good little duck did so, and when they were safely across and had walked for a short time, the forest seemed to be more and more familiar to them, and at length they saw from afar their father’s house. Then they began to run, rushed into the parlor, and threw themselves into their father’s arms. The man had not known one happy hour since he had left the children in the forest; the woman, however, was dead. Gretel emptied her pinafore until pearls and precious stones ran about the room, and Hansel threw one handful after another out of his pocket to add to them.
